metric_defs.name: Composite
metric_defs.means: Mean of available judge, F1, EM, contains. Default ranker — blends generative and extractive pressure.

metric_defs.name: Generative lens
metric_defs.means: Judge + contains. Fairer to GraphRAG prose that humans accept but Hotpot F1 punishes.

metric_defs.name: Extractive lens
metric_defs.means: Token F1 + EM. Classic Hotpot scoring. Prefer when answers must be short spans.

metric_defs.name: LLM judge
metric_defs.means: Semantic correctness vs gold. Correlates better with humans than EM on generative QA, but is not faithfulness-to-context.

metric_defs.name: Tokens / query
metric_defs.means: Cost proxy. Graph global / frontier often win quality on some slices while burning tokens.

metric_map.note: Local judge scores usefulness vs gold. Not identical to RAGAS answer_relevancy (query-conditioned, often reference-free).
2026 guides treat faithfulness as mandatory. This bake-off does not yet score claim-vs-context; do not equate judge with faithfulness.
Separate retrieval eval (nDCG@k, recall@k) is standard in CodeRAG-Bench and GraphRAG-Bench. End-to-end scores alone hide retrieval failures.
Hotpot-style. Underestimates fluent paraphrases (Qi 2025; LLM-as-judge reassessments 2025).
Loose check that gold (or code body tokens) appear in the prediction.
Production selection is multi-objective — quality alone is not a ship decision (Braintrust / Atlan 2026 practice).

research_findings.claim: No single RAG paradigm wins everywhere
research_findings.evidence: Unified evaluations (RAG vs GraphRAG systematic studies, 2025–26) and GraphRAG-Bench show vector RAG competitive on fact lookup; graphs pull ahead on complex reasoning / contextual summarize. Hybrid or routed stacks beat either alone.
research_findings.dashboard: Use Decision Lab → generative vs extractive + routing table; don’t pick from one bar chart.

research_findings.evidence: RAGAS / DeepEval / 2026 guides: a pipeline can look ‘faithful’ while context recall quietly collapses. CodeRAG-Bench explicitly reports retrieval nDCG and end-to-end gen.
research_findings.dashboard: Metric map marks context precision/recall as gaps — treat end-to-end ranks as provisional.

research_findings.evidence: Hotpot-style extractive metrics penalize correct verbose answers. LLM-as-judge closes much of the gap to human ratings; dual scoreboards routinely flip winners.
research_findings.dashboard: Dual scoreboard + Generative vs Extractive scatter are first-class, not footnotes.

research_findings.claim: Code RAG bottleneck is often retrieval, not generation
research_findings.evidence: CodeRAG-Bench: gold docs help even strong models; current retrievers struggle on DS-1000 / ODEX / SWE-style tasks. Leave-gold-out is required for honest basic-programming eval.
research_findings.dashboard: CodeRAG card explains leave-gold-out; expand scored n before claiming production readiness.

research_findings.claim: Ship a router, not a religion
research_findings.evidence: Industry + academic synthesis 2026: route local factoids to vector+rerank; reserve graph / frontier for multi-hop or corpus-wide synthesis; watch token/latency SLOs.
research_findings.dashboard: Routing recommendations + Pareto (quality vs tokens) encode that tradeoff.

method_defs.Semantic: Dense vector retrieve + generate. Strong baseline for single-hop / local factoids.
method_defs.Rerank: Retrieve then rerank. Often best quality/latency interactive path in this harness.
method_defs.BM25+dense: Sparse+dense fusion. Helps keyword-heavy queries; paper-standard hybrid retriever.
method_defs.Hybrid: Vector + graph local path in this harness.
method_defs.GraphRAG fast/basic: Fast NLP graph index + basic/local search. Often high generative / contains, low F1.
method_defs.GraphRAG global: Community-summary global search. Costly; for corpus-wide themes, not factoids.
method_defs.Frontier: Adaptive + corrective-style stack — multi-hop candidate in routing table.

benches.title: HotpotQA distractor
benches.what: Multi-hop Wikipedia QA (distractor). Gold answers are short extractive spans. Recent critiques (Qi 2025) note EM/F1 punish fluent generative answers that humans accept — which is why this dashboard always shows generative vs extractive lenses.
benches.how_to_read: Prefer composite for a balanced rank; check generative if your UX is chatty prose; check extractive if you need short-span fidelity. Ranking flips are expected.

meta.note: Full distractor validation = 7405 hard Q / ~66k paragraphs. Local GraphRAG runs are practical at n≈100–500; use n=all only with vector-only methods or a large compute budget.

benches.briefing:
# Engineering scorecard

Default interactive path: **Vector + rerank**
- Reason: Best quality among methods with p95 ≤ 5.0s
- Quality: 0.426 | usable: 75%
- p95 latency: 2.70s | tokens/query: 1265

## Routing (by scenario)
- **multi_hop** → FrontierRAG (adaptive+CRAG) (q=0.406, 2059 tok/q) — Bridge / cross-doc multi-hop → FrontierRAG (adaptive+CRAG).
- **local_factoid** → Vector + rerank (q=0.557, 1265 tok/q) — Single-entity / comparison factoids → Vector + rerank. H2H 1W-1L vs runner-up (meanΔ=0.021; treat as soft)

## Recommendations
- Ship a query router, not one RAG stack: local factoids vs multi-hop need different paths.
- MULTI_HOP: FrontierRAG (adaptive+CRAG) (q=0.41, Δ=0.05, 2059 tok/q).
- LOCAL_FACTOID: Vector + rerank (q=0.56, Δ=0.02, 1265 tok/q).
- Usable-answer leader (GraphRAG fast/basic, 83%) differs from composite leader (Vector + rerank) — pick the metric that matches your UX.
- Highest token cost: FrontierRAG (adaptive+CRAG) (2059 tok/q) — gate behind hard-query classifier.
- Misses p95≤5.0s SLO: GraphRAG global, GraphRAG local, Hybrid (vec+graph local), GraphRAG fast/basic, Adaptive router, FrontierRAG (adaptive+CRAG). Keep interactive path on vector; run graph/hybrid async or on stronger GPUs.
- Rebuild GraphRAG indexes only on corpus change; amortize index_seconds over expected volume.

## Caveats
- Eval set size n=12 — treat rankings as directional, not production SLAs.
- Overlapping quality CIs are common at this n; trust large gaps (latency/tokens/local EM) over 0.01 composite deltas.
- Composite mixes EM/F1/judge; generative graph answers often lose on EM even when useful.
- Absolute latency depends on hardware + model size; use relative ordering for stack choice.
- Graph index build dominates cold-start cost; measure amortized $/query at your QPS.

benches.title: CodeRAG-Bench
benches.what: Wang et al.: retrieval-augmented code generation across basic programming and open-domain tasks. Canonical solutions are leave-gold-out. Paper finding: high-quality context helps, but retrievers often fail to fetch it — end-to-end RAG ≠ oracle RAG.
benches.how_to_read: Code-aware contains/judge matter more than wiki-style F1. Compare methods under the same datastore; do not treat token F1 as pass@k.
benches.paper: Wang et al., Findings NAACL 2025 · https://code-rag-bench.github.io/

meta.source: humaneval + mbpp + ds1000 + odex · programming-solutions + library-documentation
meta.protocol: Leave-gold-out for HumanEval/MBPP solutions; open-domain tasks retrieve against library docs (± StackOverflow).
meta.note: Full CodeRAG-Bench also includes RepoEval / SWE-bench-Lite / CodeSearchNet-Py (repo-level + retrieval). This harness ships the complete basic + open-domain categories (~2.1k Q / ~35k docs).

benches.title: GraphRAG-Bench Novel
benches.what: Built to answer: when do graph structures help? Tasks scale from fact retrieval → complex reasoning → contextual summarize → creative generation. Literature: graphs often tie or lose on L1 fact lookup; gains concentrate on harder reasoning/summarize.
benches.how_to_read: Do not crown GraphRAG from Hotpot averages alone. Filter by question type here; expect vector methods to compete on factoid items.
benches.paper: Xiang et al., When to use Graphs in RAG · https://github.com/GraphRAG-Bench/GraphRAG-Benchmark

findings.obs1: Basic RAG matches GraphRAG on Fact Retrieval
findings.obs2: GraphRAG excels on Complex Reasoning / Summarize / Creative
